artifacts.title: Warhammer Age of Sigmar: The Rules
Warhammer Age of Sigmar Rules Updates

structuralEvidence.subject: phase-independent-reaction-window
structuralEvidence.finding: Reaction timing is tied to the triggering ability-resolution sequence and does not require a named turn phase.

structuralEvidence.subject: stormcast-ruination-reaction
structuralEvidence.finding: The current Stormcast Eternals erratum identifies Ruination Chamber as a once-per-turn Army reaction triggered when the unit is targeted by a non-Core ability.

structuralEvidence.subject: phase-independent-active-window
structuralEvidence.finding: The current Nighthaunt update replaces the Pyregheists' older End of Any Turn timing with usage-only Once Per Turn (Army), so the active ability has no named phase and must not inherit the stale source phase.

structuralEvidence.subject: lumineth-multiple-parts-passive
structuralEvidence.finding: The current Lumineth Realm-lords update adds Multiple Parts to the Sanctum of Amyntok with Passive timing, identifying the authoritative value for a candidate export row whose condition is empty and whose ability_phase metadata says Start of Turn; formal reconciliation is still required.

notes: All three official PDFs extracted without diagnostics under the bounded page and text limits.
The checked-in report contains locators and checksums but no page text.
The current June 2026 update from the live downloads index was reviewed with the base rules when defining the reaction window.
Its Stormcast Eternals erratum corroborates the explicit Reaction text on both remaining contradictory candidate rows.
The current Nighthaunt update supersedes the September 2024 phase for Light a Pyre; the Wahapedia CSV condition is current while its separate ability_phase column is stale.
The current Lumineth Realm-lords update supplies the Passive timing omitted from the Multiple Parts export row; the candidate remains blocked until formal reconciliation links both source records.
